question: How do classical logical diagnosis, abduction, structural actual causality, counterfactual feature changes, responsibility, and Shapley attribution connect, and what role can declarative reasoning play in constrained XAI?

key_findings.claim: The article gives a useful conceptual bridge from model-based diagnosis and abduction to modern local prediction explanations.
key_findings.evidence: A running Boolean-circuit example shows consistency-based diagnosis as restoring consistency by marking components abnormal, abduction as adding minimal facts that entail an observation, and actual causality as testing interventions under contingencies. The same logic is then transferred to database query causes and black-box classifier feature changes.

key_findings.claim: Generalized Resp combines minimal counterfactual contingencies with the expected label change from resampling a focal feature.
key_findings.evidence: For an entity e and feature F, it holds a contingency assignment fixed, averages the binary label after replacing F over its domain, divides the original-minus-expected label by one plus contingency size, then maximizes among the smallest contingencies with positive effect. This distinguishes features whose individual changes flip the classifier at different rates and extends binary Halpern-Chockler responsibility.

key_findings.claim: Black-box feature replacement and actual causation are not interchangeable without a structural causal model.
key_findings.evidence: The early causality section correctly notes that causal directions, endogenous variables, and structural equations are required. Yet the classifier section calls arbitrary input-value substitutions and generalized Resp 'causal' while using only the input/output map. Such perturbations establish model sensitivity under a chosen reference distribution; they do not show that changing the real-world feature would cause either the predictor input or the desired outcome to change.

key_findings.claim: The generalized responsibility definition encodes strong normative choices that can dominate its ranking.
key_findings.evidence: It first minimizes contingency cardinality and only then maximizes expected label change. A feature with an arbitrarily tiny positive single-feature effect therefore outranks a feature with a much larger effect that manifests through a two-feature interaction. Scores also depend on feature-domain granularity, value distribution, mutable-feature policy, and which correlated combinations are admitted; none of these is determined by the classifier itself.

key_findings.claim: The SHAP presentation is specifically conditional-expectation SHAP, not a unique distribution-free notion of feature contribution.
key_findings.evidence: The game value G_e(S)=E[L(e') | e'_S=e_S] conditions on observed feature coalitions. Conditional, interventional/marginal, baseline, and causal graph-based Shapley games can disagree under dependence and satisfy different axioms. The article notes distribution dependence but does not foreground that the Shapley uniqueness theorem applies only after the game function has been chosen.

key_findings.claim: Exact attribution can be polynomial for compiled deterministic-decomposable Boolean models even though it is generally counting-hard.
key_findings.evidence: The article summarizes #P-hardness of SHAP even for monotone 2-CNF under product distributions, then explains deterministic and decomposable Boolean circuits, where model-count decomposition supports polynomial SHAP algorithms. It cites efficient coverage for decision trees and related knowledge-compiled representations, while emphasizing compilation size as a separate concern.

key_findings.claim: Answer-set programming is proposed as a single declarative layer for generating, constraining, comparing, and querying counterfactuals, but this article does not evaluate scalability or explanation quality.
key_findings.evidence: ASP can express alternative interventions, inertia, minimality, actionability, domain constraints, brave/cautious queries, and interaction with external classifiers. The paper points to earlier implementations for responsibility and database causes and notes probabilistic ASP may be needed for expectation-based scores. It supplies no new algorithm, benchmark, runtime, user study, fidelity test, or comparison in this article.

method.core_idea: Use simple logical examples to unify several traditions of explanation, formalize feature responsibility and conditional SHAP as counterfactual attribution scores, summarize their computational complexity, and advocate answer-set programming for domain-aware counterfactual reasoning.
method.mechanism: Start from a logical system model plus abnormal observation; derive minimal consistency diagnoses or abductive supports; define actual causes through interventions and minimum contingencies; translate those interventions to classifier feature records; compute either generalized responsibility or a Shapley game over expected labels; exploit compiled Boolean structure for exact algorithms; and constrain/query feasible counterfactuals with ASP rules.
assumptions: The system model, abnormal components, endogenous variables, interventions, and preference order are correctly specified.
Classifier feature substitutions are meaningful counterfactual worlds rather than merely synthetic inputs.
Feature domains and a probability distribution over entities are available for expected-label scores.
Minimum contingency size is the appropriate primary measure of causal strength.
The conditional-expectation game is the intended SHAP semantics for the application.
The classifier can be queried extensively or compiled into a tractable logical representation.
Logical domain rules accurately capture feasibility, actionability, and causal dependence.
Users benefit from exact minimal logical explanations despite their computational and cognitive costs.

techniques.role: Explains abnormal behavior by minimally changing component normality assumptions to restore model consistency.
Finds minimal added hypotheses sufficient to entail an observation or prediction.
Ranks causes by the smallest contingency needed for a counterfactual outcome change.
Combines expected flip magnitude across feature values with contingency size.
Allocates the local prediction difference through a Shapley game of conditional expected labels.
Uses deterministic decomposable circuit structure for tractable exact counting and attribution.
Specifies feasible interventions, minimality, domain constraints, and counterfactual queries declaratively.

limitations: This is a selective expository article, explicitly not an exhaustive survey, and contributes no new experiment or algorithm.
It sometimes blurs classifier counterfactual sensitivity, structural causal explanation, and actionable recourse.
Only conditional-expectation SHAP is formalized despite materially different SHAP games.
Generalized Resp's lexicographic minimum-contingency preference is not justified against alternative causal-effect or user-utility objectives.
Continuous and high-cardinality feature domains make the expectation and exhaustive contingency search underspecified or infeasible.
Feasibility constraints can prevent absurd counterfactuals but do not by themselves supply causal transition dynamics.
The tractable-circuit discussion does not quantify compilation blow-up or end-to-end cost for learned models.
ASP scalability, probabilistic inference, model integration, and explanation stability are referred to prior work rather than assessed here.
No human-grounded evaluation establishes that logically minimal or high-scoring explanations are understandable or useful.
The running loan example risks treating immutable identity and socially coupled features as freely replaceable until constraints are added later.
failure_modes: Conditioning on correlated features can assign importance to a feature the predictor never uses.
Marginal/interventional replacement can create off-support records on which classifier behavior is arbitrary.
A prediction-flipping edit can game the classifier without improving the person's real outcome.
An incomplete causal graph or domain rule set can certify harmful or impossible recourse as actionable.
Discretizing a continuous feature more finely changes generalized Resp by changing its averaging measure.
Exact subset enumeration becomes exponential in feature count, and compiled circuits can grow exponentially.
Multiple equally minimal diagnoses or counterfactuals can leave users without a principled choice.
Minimum-cardinality explanations can omit distributed evidence and be unstable under small model/data changes.
Protected or proxy features can receive high attribution without clarifying discrimination, remediation, or legal relevance.
A black-box I/O relation cannot identify causal direction or distinguish intervention from association.
reusable_insights: Specify the explanation target first: model behavior, data association, real-world outcome, diagnosis, or recourse require different semantics.
Make the background distribution, baseline, allowed interventions, causal model, and minimality preference part of the explanation object.
Use logical constraints to exclude impossible counterfactuals, but use structural equations or transition models for causal action effects.
Exploit model structure and knowledge compilation when exact attribution is required; report compilation cost separately.
Expose several Pareto-optimal counterfactuals across cost, feasibility, probability of success, and robustness rather than one cardinality minimum.
Treat SHAP as a family indexed by a game function, not a uniquely determined universal feature importance.
Pair score computation with queries that reveal which counterfactual worlds and contingencies generated the number.
open_questions: Which explanation semantics best match distinct user tasks such as auditing, debugging, scientific causation, and recourse?
How can ASP constraints and uncertain structural causal models be combined at practical scale?
Can generalized Resp be axiomatized and compared with conditional, interventional, baseline, and causal Shapley values?
How stable are minimum contingencies under model retraining, measurement error, and distribution shift?
What compilation classes yield end-to-end tractability for modern ensembles and neural networks without exponential blow-up?
How should costs, protected attributes, downstream side effects, and probability of successful recourse enter counterfactual rankings?
Can exact logical explanations be compressed into human-usable summaries without losing their guarantees?
How should explanation systems communicate causal ignorance rather than presenting input edits as causes?

competitive_landscape.title: A Unified Approach to Interpreting Model Predictions
competitive_landscape.difference: Lundberg and Lee formalize additive feature attribution and efficient SHAP approximations. Bertossi places one conditional-expectation version beside causal responsibility and logic, emphasizing exact complexity and counterfactual reasoning rather than approximation performance or user studies.

competitive_landscape.title: The Many Shapley Values for Model Explanation
competitive_landscape.difference: Sundararajan and Najmi distinguish baseline, random-baseline, and conditional-expectation games and show the usual uniqueness argument does not choose among them. This directly qualifies the article's singular presentation of 'the Shap score' and makes the distribution/game choice central.

competitive_landscape.title: Predictive and Causal Implications of Using Shapley Value for Model Interpretation
competitive_landscape.difference: Ma and Tourani analyze Shapley values in Bayesian networks and show feature attribution need not reflect causal relations or safe feature removal. Their result sharpens the distinction this exposition sometimes blurs between attribution under a distribution and actual causality under interventions.

competitive_landscape.title: Abduction-Based Explanations for Machine Learning Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Ignatiev et al. compile models to constraints and compute subset- or cardinality-minimal sufficient explanations with formal guarantees and benchmark evidence. This article explains the abduction connection more broadly and advocates ASP, but provides no new scalability evaluation.

competitive_landscape.title: Algorithmic Recourse under Imperfect Causal Knowledge: a Probabilistic Approach
competitive_landscape.difference: Karimi et al. prove guaranteed recourse is impossible without true structural equations and optimize probabilistic counterfactual or subpopulation interventions under causal uncertainty. Bertossi's ASP proposal is stronger for declarative constraints and queries but does not resolve causal-model uncertainty or validate action success.

competitive_landscape.title: On the Computational Tractability of the (Many) Shapley Values
competitive_landscape.difference: Marzouk et al. separately map local/global conditional, interventional, and baseline SHAP complexity across model and distribution classes, including tractability under Hidden Markov distributions and new tree/neural hardness. This extends the article's complexity discussion beyond conditional SHAP and deterministic-decomposable circuits.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Classical logical explanation, causal responsibility, counterfactual feature attribution, SHAP complexity, and answer-set reasoning form a coherent lineage that can enrich modern XAI with explicit reasoning.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper gives unusually accessible cross-field examples, a detailed generalized responsibility definition, a compact knowledge-compilation account, and concrete categories of counterfactual queries and constraints.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Its value is pedagogical synthesis rather than a new method or evaluation. The logic-to-XAI bridge is useful, but the exposition should more sharply separate sensitivity from structural causation, prediction flips from successful recourse, and conditional SHAP from other Shapley games. Those distinctions determine whether the proposed explanations answer the user's real question.

reviewer_notes: Read all 22 pages, including every logical/database/classifier example, generalized Resp construction, SHAP equations and complexity claims, deterministic-decomposable circuit discussion, ASP proposal, and references. Checked primary NeurIPS, ICML/AISTATS PMLR, AAAI, and causal-recourse sources through 2026-08-23.
